title: Best Speak Competitors & Alternatives in August 2026
summary: Need more than Speak's guided curriculum? August 2026 roundup ranked on turn detection, memory, and vocabulary review.
body_markdown:
There's a specific frustration that shows up around the intermediate stage: you can get through Speak's lessons fine, but an unscripted conversation still throws you. That gap between completing a unit and actually speaking freely is a structural one, and swapping apps is sometimes the right call. Here are the alternatives that hold up when the guided format stops being enough.


**TLDR:**


- Speak works for beginners who want a guided curriculum, but its scripted format gives intermediate learners nowhere to go once they outgrow it
- The three gaps that matter most when you move past Speak: no smart turn detection, no cross-session memory, and no vocabulary review tied to sentences you actually spoke
- Cheaper sticker prices only win if you practice as often as the pricier option; Langotalk at $6.67 used twice a week costs the same per session as ISSEN at $25 used daily
- Talkpal covers 57+ languages if your target language isn't available elsewhere; Loora covers English professionals; Duolingo covers early vocabulary through daily streaks
- ISSEN is a real-time voice tutor built around the three gaps Speak leaves open, with sessions that start in under 30 seconds and a free 10-minute trial


## What is Speak and how does it work?


Speak (built by Speakeasy Labs) is a mobile-first[language learning app for speaking](https://www.issen.com/blog/best-language-learning-apps-speaking/) organized around a three-step loop: short video lessons that introduce target phrases, speaking drills with word-by-word emphasis, and scenario-based roleplays where an AI tutor gives you tasks like ordering at a cafe or making travel plans.


Lessons are grouped into thematic units. Each unit stacks tutor-led video segments, sentence repetition exercises, and a capstone roleplay that pushes you to apply phrases in a simulated exchange. The curriculum is guided and linear, giving beginners a clear path from one topic to the next.


On the App Store, Speak lists English and 15 additional languages, with pricing at $17.99 per month or $83.99 annually. The English curriculum is the deepest by a wide margin, and the American English tutor voice and video-first format signal who it was built for.


### Who Speak fits best


- Beginners and lower-intermediate learners who want a structured curriculum work best inside Speak's format.
- Learners who prefer watching short lessons and repeating scripted phrases over open-ended conversation.
- English learners in particular, given the depth of the English track compared to other supported languages.


## Why consider Speak alternatives?


Speak works well inside a narrow band of use cases. Outside that band, the gaps show up quickly.


### Where Speak falls short


- Conversation depth is thin. In[independent testing across multiple apps](https://lingtuitive.com/blog/best-ai-speaking-apps) , Speak felt more like answering questions than a back-and-forth, and the AI sometimes decided the conversation was over with no way to push further.
- Advanced learners hit a ceiling. Reviewers note that some lessons skew too basic past the intermediate band, and the roleplay format rewards scripted phrases over spontaneous production.
- No cross-session memory, based on current app store listings and reviewer testing. The tutor does not carry your interests, prior stumbles, or goals from one session to the next.
- No smart turn detection. Turns feel more like prompt-and-response than[natural AI speaking practice](https://www.issen.com/blog/how-ai-speaking-practice-works/) .
- No conversation-anchored SRS. Vocabulary review sits separate from the sentences you actually produced.
- No[dedicated shadowing mode](https://www.issen.com/blog/shadowing-pronunciation-technique/) . Pronunciation work happens inside scripted drills, not a focused pause-and-repeat environment with multiple regional accents.
- Pricing at[$17.99 per month or $83.99 annually](https://speakshark.com/blog/speak-app-review-2026) is competitive, but value drops sharply if you outgrow the beginner curriculum within a few months.


If you are past the guided-curriculum stage and need volume, memory, and unpredictability, Speak is structurally the wrong tool.


## Best Speak alternatives in August 2026


### ISSEN: best overall Speak alternative


ISSEN is a real-time[AI voice tutor for language learning](https://www.issen.com/blog/best-ai-voice-tutors-language-learning/) on iOS, Android, and web that runs open conversations in 60+ languages, adapts difficulty within each turn, and builds vocabulary through flashcards anchored to sentences you actually spoke.


What it does well:


- Smart turn detection for natural voice exchange, no push-to-talk
- [Conversation-anchored SRS](https://www.issen.com/blog/spaced-repetition-vocabulary-ai-conversation-practice/) that surfaces each word in its original spoken context
- Dedicated Shadowing mode across American, British, Australian, Argentinian, Mexican, and Castilian accents
- Background and lock-screen mode for hands-free reps on walks or commutes
- Cross-session memory that tracks interests, prior stumbles, and topics
- Multilingual conversation support (e.g., Spanglish)


Best for: post-beginner learners (B1+) who need daily speaking volume and tutor-driven open conversation.


Bottom line: where Speak's guided format tops out, ISSEN takes over with unlimited on-demand sessions that start in under 30 seconds.


### Loora


Loora is an AI-powered English speaking tutor with real-time voice conversations on iOS, Android, and web, with role-play scenarios covering interviews and meetings. Pronunciation notes arrive post-session.


Best for: B1+ professionals focused on English at work.


Where it falls short: Loora focuses solely on English, and lacks smart turn detection, conversation-anchored SRS, a dedicated shadowing mode, cross-session memory, and background mode.


Bottom line: credible English-only tutor, but ISSEN wins on language range and structural features.


### Langotalk


Langotalk offers AI conversations in 19+ languages, available on web and mobile. At $6.67/month annually, it undercuts most competitors.


Best for: budget-conscious learners wanting multi-language reps.


Where it falls short: no smart turn detection, no conversation-anchored SRS, no dedicated shadowing mode, no cross-session memory.


Bottom line: cheapest broad-language option, but shallower on adaptive tutoring than ISSEN.


### Praktika


Praktika uses an immersive 3D avatar English system and skips grammar drills for immersive roleplay.


Best for: visual learners who want character-driven English scenario practice.


Where it falls short: B2+ learners may exhaust scenarios. No smart turn detection, no conversation-anchored SRS, no dedicated shadowing mode, no cross-session memory, no background mode.


Bottom line: engaging for scripted scenarios, limited for open-ended adaptive talk.


*Note: the table lists Praktika's web app availability as No. Verify on Praktika's live site before publishing, as this was not confirmed by the cited source.*


### Talkpal


Talkpal's 57+ languages is the widest selection here, with chat, role-plays, debates, and exercises.


Best for: learners studying less common languages.


Where it falls short: voices sound more synthetic, and it lacks smart turn detection, conversation-anchored SRS, a dedicated shadowing mode, and cross-session memory.


Bottom line: pick Talkpal when language availability is the binding constraint; otherwise ISSEN wins on conversation quality.


### Duolingo


Duolingo is a gamified app built around short daily exercises and streaks. Its Max tier adds Video Call and Roleplay in German, Spanish, French, Italian, and Portuguese, though these stay guided and predictable.


Best for: beginners building early vocabulary through daily habits.


Where it falls short:[gamified apps](https://www.issen.com/blog/beyond-gamified-apps-speaking-fluency/) optimize for 5-10 minutes of streak maintenance, not the spoken output volume needed for active fluency.


Bottom line: useful for early vocabulary; ISSEN takes over where conversation depth is required.

## FAQs


### Why do advanced learners look for Speak alternatives?


Speak's guided curriculum works well for beginners, but past the intermediate band, the scripted roleplay format stops generating the unpredictable conversational pressure that builds real fluency. Reviewers consistently note that lessons skew too basic at higher levels, and the tutor carries no memory of your prior sessions, so each conversation starts from zero.


### What features should you focus on when comparing Speak alternatives for speaking practice?


Look for smart turn detection (so conversation flows naturally without push-to-talk), cross-session memory (so the tutor builds on what you practiced before), and conversation-anchored vocabulary review (so the words you review come from sentences you actually spoke). These three gaps are precisely what Speak's current architecture does not fill.


### When does switching from Speak to ISSEN make sense?


If you have finished Speak's beginner curriculum and find yourself answering scripted prompts instead of holding an open conversation, that is the structural signal to switch. ISSEN is built for post-beginner learners (B1 and above) who need daily speaking volume with a tutor that adapts mid-turn and remembers you across sessions.


### Is ISSEN more expensive than Speak for daily practice?


At face value, Speak at $17.99 per month looks cheaper than ISSEN at $20 to $29 per month. Reframe by session frequency: a learner using Speak twice a week pays roughly $2.25 per session, while a learner using ISSEN daily pays closer to $0.83 per session, with each session running unlimited in length instead of capping out at a scripted unit.


### Can you use ISSEN alongside Speak, or does it replace it entirely?


For beginners, Speak's structured unit-by-unit curriculum and ISSEN's open conversation practice can complement each other, with Speak supplying the lesson scaffolding and ISSEN supplying the speaking reps. Once you outgrow Speak's guided format, ISSEN functions as a standalone daily practice layer, and you can try it free for 10 minutes to see whether the open-conversation format fits where you are now.
